steps.userMessage:
MEMENTO | Heirloom carnelian pendant reset

I want one pendant that lets an inherited carved stone remain the focus of an everyday piece. G1 is the single reddish carnelian intaglio in stone-front.jpg, recorded by The Metropolitan Museum of Art as object 244973, accession 81.6.102, Gift of John Taylor Johnston, 1881. Its published overall dimensions are 1.3 × 0.9 × 0.4 cm; the design basis is a nominal 13 × 9 × 4 mm envelope. Preserve its irregular oval outline, existing small edge losses, translucent red body and incised figure/chariot/serpent scene. The carved face faces outward. engraving-impression.jpg supplies a grey, mirrored positive reading of that carving; stone-front.jpg supplies the gemstone’s appearance.

Develop a new setting, bail and coordinating chain in 925 silver, with polished, satin or oxidized finishes in locations you choose. G1 remains one intact stone with its existing surfaces and edge losses. Give it visible mechanical support and retention around the perimeter, with the central engraved scene readable. The pendant including its bail fits within 30 mm high × 24 mm wide × 10 mm deep. Choose one chain length from 420–500 mm and a generic silver clasp. The same adult wearer appears in W1, an open neckline with the pendant against the upper chest, and W2, a fine knit top with the pendant on the fabric. Print "MEMENTO" on all six boards and "925 silver" on the specification and stone-to-setting boards.

Audience: the holder choosing a daily-wear redesign and the jeweller reviewing its proportions and mounting arrangement.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the stone record, silver specification, dimensional limits and wearing contexts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the six deliverables with their proportions, formats and stages. stone-front.jpg is the identity image for G1’s carved face, colour, outline and edge losses. engraving-impression.jpg is a reference for reading the carving through its mirrored positive impression. stone-envelope.png is the constraint drawing of the nominal stone envelope and pendant size limits. everyday-neckline.png is an atmosphere reference for the two clothing contexts and upper-torso framing.

Deliverables:
1. One finished pendant overview board with an enlarged three-quarter view and the complete coordinating chain, bail and clasp
2. One orthographic board with aligned front, side and rear views, the chosen pendant height, width and depth, and the separate nominal G1 envelope
3. One stone-to-setting board with an exploded relationship view and a section identifying stone contact regions, perimeter retention and the nominal stone envelope
4. One final specification board recording G1’s identity and nominal dimensions, the chosen pendant dimensions, chain length, 925 silver components, finish locations and clasp arrangement
5. One W1 wearing board with an open neckline, the pendant against the upper chest, its chain attachment visible and the chosen chain length stated
6. One W2 wearing board with the same adult wearer and pendant on a fine knit top, its chain attachment visible and the same chain length stated

Acceptance:
- The overview, orthographic and stone-to-setting boards depict the same single G1, preserving the irregular oval outline, edge losses, red translucency and engraved scene in stone-front.jpg; the specification board records its nominal 13 × 9 × 4 mm envelope separately from the new metalwork.
- The orthographic and specification boards state matching pendant dimensions within 30 mm high × 24 mm wide × 10 mm deep, including the bail; the stone-to-setting board labels the stone geometry basis as "Nominal stone envelope" wherever a section or hidden surface is represented.
- The overview, orthographic and stone-to-setting boards agree on bail position, metal backing and perimeter retention; the stone-to-setting board identifies mechanical supports and contact regions while leaving the central engraved scene readable.
- The specification board assigns polished, satin or oxidized finishes to the 925 silver setting, bail and chain; the overview and both wearing boards reproduce those assignments and the same clasp arrangement. The specification and stone-to-setting boards print "925 silver".
- The W1 and W2 wearing boards show the full pendant, chain attachment and enough neck and torso to judge scale, with a small pendant close-up wherever the carving needs enlargement; both carry their context label and the same 420–500 mm chain length recorded on the specification board.
- All six boards print "MEMENTO"; the overview, orthographic, stone-to-setting and wearing boards retain the outward-facing carved face and the proportions recorded on the specification board.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
